subject: Media Literacy
title: Slowing Down Before Sharing
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Slowing Down Before Sharing.

hook.text: MIT found that false news stories spread six times faster than true ones on social media.

buildup.text: The impulse to share outrageous news instantly is powerful — but speed is the enemy of accuracy.

discovery.text: Simply pausing to read beyond the headline before sharing reduces misinformation spread dramatically.

twist.text: Platforms know this but don't add friction because friction reduces engagement — and engagement means revenue.

climax.text: The most powerful thing you can do for media quality is pause before you share.

punchline.text: Read it first. Share it second. Or don't share it at all.

quiz.question: According to MIT research, how much faster does false news spread than true news?
